plain_summary: Review a benzodiazepine at age 65 or older when sleep apnoea is documented.

medicine_groups.name: Benzodiazepines
medicine_groups.note: A single supply is enough. Z-drugs are outside the printed class.

needs_facts.meets: A diagnosis of sleep apnoea that applies at the time of benzodiazepine supply.

options.words: Sleep apnoea was present at the time of the benzodiazepine supply
Sleep apnoea was absent at the time of the benzodiazepine supply

rule_for_models: At age 65 or older, give a finding for a Group A benzodiazepine supply with sleep apnoea documented at supply, whatever the indication. Cite the medicine and diagnosis. Asthma or COPD alone does not qualify. Z-drugs are excluded. Give no finding below age 65 or if sleep apnoea is ruled out. If age, exposure or sleep apnoea status is unclear and the other evidence fits, report only a possible finding naming the missing evidence. Ask whether sleep apnoea had been diagnosed by the time of this supply. If its timing is unknown, keep the finding possible.
cannot_be_seen: Dispensing does not establish actual use, indication or a prescriber’s intent. Treatment and assessments elsewhere may be missing.
ask_the_gp: Could you confirm whether the patient has sleep apnoea and review whether the benzodiazepine remains suitable? If the benzodiazepine is still being used and sleep apnoea is confirmed, could we review it today before the next dose?
